title: Dry-fit a slip coupling across the open joint of a drain-pipe repair
instruction: Dry-fit the second repair coupling across the open joint, centred on the witness marks, then let go.
context: Replacing a cracked length of drain pipe is everyday work for plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (about 500,000 in the US) and general maintenance and repair workers (about 1.5 million). Every joint is dry-fitted before cementing. A repair coupling has no centre stop, so it slides along the pipe with little play; the loose new length sags in its dry joint, and the coupling will not pass onto it unless that end is held up in line.
setup: Positions from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are measured from the midline between them, and heights are above the table top. A white 1-1/2 in Schedule 40 PVC drain line (48.3 mm outside diameter) runs straight away from the robot on the midline, with its axis 90 mm up. A length has been cut out of it, leaving a 220 mm gap from 18.2 to 40.2 cm in front. The two fixed ends rest on saddles in steel pipe clamps, on 16 mm posts with foot plates, at 7.2 and 51.5 cm. The near end starts at 4.5 cm and the far end stops at 55 cm. A loose replacement length (white PVC, 212 mm, 153 g) fills the gap, 4 mm short of each fixed end. Both of its cut ends are bevelled on the outside, 2 mm deep at 30 degrees. Two loose grey PVC repair couplings (80 g each) have no centre stop: each is 80 mm long, with a bore of 48.7 mm (0.2 mm of play per side), 57.5 mm outside, and both mouths bevelled 2 mm deep at 30 degrees. One sits centred on the far joint, from 36.0 to 44.0 cm. The replacement's near end hangs in its play, about 6.5 mm low. The other coupling is slid fully back onto the near fixed end, from 9.6 to 17.6 cm, its mouth 6 mm short of the cut. Black witness marks 4 mm wide are drawn round the pipes 38 mm from each pipe end, at 14.4, 22.4, 36.0 and 44.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end, with both grippers at least 5 mm from the replacement and both couplings, and all three still. A depth is how far a pipe end reaches inside a coupling, measured from the coupling's mouth. No credit unless all of these hold: both ends of the replacement are within 1.5 mm of the line's axis; the replacement is within 1 degree of the line; the far coupling is on the line (its middle within 1.5 mm of the axis and within 1 degree), with both of its pipes at least 30 mm inside it; and the near coupling is on the line in the same way. 1.0: the near fixed end and the replacement are each at least 32 mm inside the near coupling, and the two depths are within 6 mm of each other, so its mouths sit on the witness marks. 0.5: each is at least 15 mm inside, but not centred. 0 otherwise, including a coupling still held. Full score counts once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: 1. Lay the replacement in the gap 4 mm from each fixed end, with its far end centred in the far coupling (the coupling's mouths on the marks at 36.0 and 44.0 cm). Let its near end hang. 2. Slide the near coupling back along the near fixed end until its mouth is 6 mm short of the cut (from 9.6 to 17.6 cm). 3. Nothing is cemented or consumed.
fidelity: True size, with real clearances. The couplings are 24-sided staves and the pipes faceted cylinders, all rigid, with dry PVC friction (0.4). The faceting lets the loose length hang about 6.5 mm low at its free end; a true round bore would give about 2 mm. Only contact holds the replacement: one dry joint at the start, two at the end. The line is level; a real drain slopes about 1.2 degrees. Dry fit only, with no primer or cement. Fixed layout, as the board asks.
